chalisa.do1: Victory to Gaṇapati, abode of virtues, with the face of a noble elephant, the compassionate one.
Victory, victory to the son of Girijā, remover of obstacles and bringer of good.
chalisa.cau1: Victory, victory, victory to Gaṇapati, king of the gaṇas, who fills all with good and brings auspicious works to pass.
chalisa.cau2: Victory to the elephant-faced one, home of happiness and giver of joy, Vināyaka of the world, bestower of wisdom.
chalisa.cau3: Your curved mouth and pure trunk are lovely; the three-lined tilaka on your forehead delights the mind.
chalisa.cau4: A garland of gems and pearls shines on your chest; a golden crown is on your head, and your eyes are large.
chalisa.cau5: In your hands are a book, an axe and a trident; you are offered modakas and fragrant flowers.
chalisa.cau6: A yellow garment adorns your handsome body; the sandals of your feet are enthroned in the minds of sages.
chalisa.cau7: Blessed son of Śiva, brother of the six-faced Kārttikeya, Gaurī's darling, you are famed throughout the world.
chalisa.cau8: Ṛddhi and Siddhi wave the fly-whisk over you; your mount, the mouse, graces the door.
chalisa.cau9: I tell the auspicious story of your birth, most pure, purifying and bringing good.
chalisa.cau10: Once the daughter of the king of mountains performed great austerities for a son.
chalisa.cau11: When her incomparable sacrifice was complete, you arrived there in the form of a Brahmin.
chalisa.cau12: Knowing you for a guest, Gaurī was glad and served you in many ways.
chalisa.cau13: Well pleased, you granted a boon: Mother, for the austerities you have undertaken for a son,
chalisa.cau14: you shall have a son of great wisdom at this very time, without bearing him in the womb.
chalisa.cau15: He will be the leader of the gaṇas, a treasury of virtue and knowledge, worshipped first, as a form of the Lord.
chalisa.cau16: Saying this, you vanished, and appeared in the cradle in the form of a child.
chalisa.cau17: When, become an infant, you began to cry, Gaurī looked on your face and her joy knew no bounds.
chalisa.cau18: All, rapt in joy, sing songs of happiness and blessing; from the sky the gods shower flowers.
chalisa.cau19: Śiva and Umā give gifts away freely; gods and sages come to see the son.
chalisa.cau20: Seeing such joy and festive splendour, King Śani too came to see.
chalisa.cau21: Counting his own failing in his mind, Śani did not wish to look at the child.
chalisa.cau22: Some ill feeling grew in Girijā's mind, and she said: Śani, does my celebration not please you?
chalisa.cau23: Śani, hesitating, began to say: What will you gain by showing me the child?
chalisa.cau24: Umā did not believe him at heart, and she bade Śani look at the child.
chalisa.cau25: As soon as the light of Śani's sidelong glance fell on him, the child's head flew off into the sky.
chalisa.cau26: Girijā fell to the ground in anguish; that state of grief cannot be described.
chalisa.cau27: An outcry arose on Kailāsa that Śani had looked on the son and destroyed him.
chalisa.cau28: At once Viṣṇu mounted Garuḍa and went, and cutting off an elephant's head with his discus, brought it back.
chalisa.cau29: He set it on the child's body, and Śaṅkara recited the mantra of life and breathed life into him.
chalisa.cau30: Then Śiva named him Gaṇeśa and gave him the boon of being worshipped first, a treasury of wisdom.
chalisa.cau31: When Śiva set a test of wisdom, it was to go around the earth.
chalisa.cau32: The six-faced Kārttikeya set off, misled and wandering; you, sitting where you were, devised a plan with your wisdom.
chalisa.cau33: You took hold of your mother's and father's feet and went around them seven times.
chalisa.cau34: Śiva said: Blessed is Gaṇeśa, and rejoiced at heart; from the sky the gods rained down flowers in plenty.
chalisa.cau35: Not even Śeṣa with his thousand mouths can sing your glory and the greatness of your wisdom.
chalisa.cau36: I am witless, impure and sorrowful; how shall I make my prayer to you?
chalisa.cau37: Rāmasundara Prabhudāsa worships you; he lives near world-famed Prayāga, at Kakarā by Durvāsā's hermitage.
chalisa.cau38: Now, Lord, have mercy on this humble one, and grant me some of your strength and some devotion to you.
chalisa.do2: Ever-new blessings dwell in the home of whoever recites this Chālīsā of Śrī Gaṇeśa with a mind intent on him, and he wins honour in the world.
chalisa.do3: In my year one thousand and ten, on Ṛṣi Pañcamī, a Sunday,
this Chālīsā of Gaṇeśa, the embodiment of blessing, was completed.
